content: 1. Drospirenone and Ethinyl estradiol is a contraceptive agent approved by the FDA for the treatment of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), acne, and contraception. 2. Common adverse reactions include headache or migraine, menstrual irregularities, nausea or vomiting, breast pain or tenderness, and mood changes. 3. For the treatment of moderate acne vulgaris in women aged 14 years or older who have no contraindications to oral contraceptive therapy and have achieved menarche, Nikki (drospirenone and ethinyl estradiol tablets USP) 3 mg/0.02 mg is indicated. 4. Nikki should only be used for acne treatment if the patient also desires oral contraception for birth control. 5. Yaz® (drospirenone and ethinyl estradiol) should be taken orally as one active (pink) tablet daily for 24 consecutive days, followed by one inert (white) tablet daily for 4 days per menstrual cycle. 6. Therapy with Yaz® should begin either on the first day of the menstrual period or on the first Sunday after the onset of menstruation. 7. Subsequent 28-day regimens of Yaz® therapy should begin on the same day of the week as the first regimen and follow the same schedule. 8. Nikki™ (drospirenone and ethinyl estradiol tablets USP) 3 mg/0.02 mg is indicated for use by women to prevent pregnancy. 9. To achieve maximum contraceptive effectiveness, Nikki must be taken exactly as directed, in the order specified on the wallet. 10. Single missed pills should be taken as soon as remembered. 11. Patients should begin taking Nikki either on the first day of their menstrual period (Day 1 Start) or on the first Sunday after the onset of their menstrual period (Sunday Start). 12. If Nikki is first taken later than the first day of the menstrual cycle, it should not be considered effective as a contraceptive until after the first 7 consecutive days of administration. 13. Patients should use a non-hormonal contraceptive as a backup during the first 7 days of Nikki administration. 14. The possibility of ovulation and conception prior to the initiation of medication should be considered. 15. Withdrawal bleeding usually occurs within 3 days following the last active (pink) tablet. 16. If spotting or breakthrough bleeding occurs while taking Nikki, patients should continue taking the medication as directed. 17. Patients should be counseled that such bleeding is usually transient and without clinical significance; however, if bleeding persists or is prolonged, they should consult their healthcare provider. 18. If withdrawal bleeding does not occur, the possibility of pregnancy should be considered. 19. If a patient has not adhered to the prescribed dosing schedule (e.g. 20. If a patient has adhered to the prescribed regimen and misses two consecutive periods, pregnancy should be ruled out. 21. Nikki should be discontinued if pregnancy is confirmed. 22. The risk of pregnancy increases with each active (pink) tablet missed. 23. For postpartum women who do not breastfeed or after a second-trimester abortion, Nikki should be started no earlier than 4 weeks postpartum due to the increased risk of thromboembolism. 24. If a patient starts Nikki postpartum and has not yet had a period, evaluate for possible pregnancy and instruct her to use an additional method of contraception until she has taken Nikki for 7 consecutive days. 25. 26. If vomiting occurs within 3 to 4 hours after taking a tablet, it should be regarded as a missed tablet. 27. Nikki should not be prescribed to women with renal impairment, adrenal insufficiency, or a high risk of arterial or venous thrombotic diseases. 28. Examples of contraindications include women who smoke and are over age 35, have a history of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular disease, coronary artery disease, thrombotic heart conditions, uncontrolled hypertension, or diabetes mellitus with vascular disease. 29. Nikki should not be used in women with breast cancer or other estrogenor progestin-sensitive cancers, liver tumors, or liver disease. 30. Nikki should not be used during pregnancy, as there is no reason to use combined oral contraceptives (COCs) during pregnancy. 31. Nikki contains drospirenone, which has antimineralocorticoid activity and may cause hyperkalemia in high-risk patients, comparable to a 25 mg dose of spironolactone. 32. Women receiving long-term treatment with medications that may increase serum potassium concentration should have their serum potassium levels checked during the first treatment cycle. 33. Medications that may increase serum potassium include ACE inhibitors, angiotensin-II receptor antagonists, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, heparin, aldosterone antagonists, and NSAIDs. 34. Women with current or past breast cancer should not use Nikki, as breast cancer is a hormonally sensitive tumor. 35. Although some studies suggest an association between COCs and an increased risk of cervical cancer or intraepithelial neoplasia, the extent to which these findings are influenced by other factors remains controversial. 36. Nikki should be discontinued if jaundice develops, as steroid hormones may be poorly metabolized in patients with impaired liver function. 37. Acute or chronic liver function disturbances may necessitate discontinuation of COC use until liver function markers return to normal and COC causation is excluded. 38. Hepatic adenomas are associated with COC use, with an estimated attributable risk of 3.3 cases per 100,000 COC users. 39. The risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) is highest during the first year of COC use and gradually decreases after discontinuation of COC use. 40. The risk of VTE in women using COCs has been estimated to be 3 to 9 per 10,000 woman-years. 41. The risk of arterial thromboses, such as strokes and myocardial infarctions, is increased with COC use, particularly in women with other risk factors for these events. 42. Oral contraceptives must be used with caution in women with cardiovascular disease risk factors. 43. Nikki should be discontinued if there is unexplained loss of vision, proptosis, diplopia, papilledema, or retinal vascular lesions, and immediate evaluation for retinal vein thrombosis should be conducted.
